{{Short description|Geodesic maps preserve the property of having constant curvature}}
In the [[mathematical]] field of [[differential geometry]], any ([[pseudo-Riemannian manifold|pseudo]]-)[[Riemannian metric]] determines a certain class of paths known as [[geodesic]]s. '''Beltrami's theorem''', named for Italian [[mathematician]] [[Eugenio Beltrami]], is a result on the inverse problem of determining a (pseudo-)Riemannian metric from its geodesics.

It is nontrivial to see that, on any [[Riemannian manifold]] of [[constant curvature]], there are smooth coordinates relative to which all nonconstant geodesics appear as straight lines. In the ''negative curvature'' case of [[hyperbolic geometry]], this is justified by the [[Beltrami–Klein model]]. In the ''positive curvature'' case of [[spherical geometry]], it is justified by the [[gnomonic projection]]. In the language of [[projective differential geometry]], these charts show that any Riemannian manifold of constant curvature is ''locally projectively flat.'' More generally, any [[pseudo-Riemannian manifold]] of constant curvature is locally projectively flat.{{sfnm|1a1=Schouten|1y=1954|1p=292}}

Beltrami's theorem asserts the converse: any connected pseudo-Riemannian manifold which is locally projectively flat must have constant curvature.{{sfnm|1a1=do Carmo|1y=2016|1p=301|2a1=Eisenhart|2y=1926|2loc=Section 40|3a1=Schouten|3y=1954|3loc=Section VI.2|4a1=Struik|4y=1961|4loc=Section 5-3}} With the use of [[tensor calculus]], the proof is straightforward. [[Hermann Weyl]] described Beltrami's original proof (done in the two-dimensional Riemannian case) as being much more complicated.{{sfnm|1a1=Beltrami|1y=1868|2a1=Weyl|2y=1921|2loc=Footnote on p. 110}} Relative to a projectively flat chart, there are functions {{math|''&rho;''<sub>''i''</sub>}} such that the [[Christoffel symbol]]s take the form
:<math>\Gamma_{ij}^k=\rho_i\delta_j^k+\rho_j\delta_i^k.</math>
Direct calculation then shows that the [[Riemann curvature tensor]] is given by
:<math>R_{ijkl}=(\partial_i\rho_j-\partial_j\rho_i)g_{kl}+g_{jl}(\partial_i\rho_k-\rho_i\rho_k)-g_{il}(\partial_j\rho_k-\rho_j\rho_k).</math>
The curvature symmetry {{math|''R''<sub>''ijkl''</sub> + ''R''<sub>''jikl''</sub> {{=}} 0}} implies that {{math|∂<sub>''i''</sub> ''&rho;''<sub>''j''</sub> {{=}} ∂<sub>''j''</sub> ''&rho;''<sub>''i''</sub>}}. The other curvature symmetry {{math|''R''<sub>''ijkl''</sub> {{=}} ''R''<sub>''klij''</sub>}}, traced over {{mvar|i}} and {{mvar|l}}, then says that 
:<math>\partial_j\rho_k-\rho_j\rho_k=g_{jk}\frac{g^{il}(\partial_i\rho_l-\rho_i\rho_l)}{n}</math>
where {{mvar|n}} is the dimension of the manifold. It is direct to verify that the left-hand side is a (locally defined) [[Codazzi tensor]], using only the given form of the Christoffel symbols. It follows from [[Schur's lemma (Riemannian geometry)|Schur's lemma]] that {{math|''g''<sup>''il''</sup>(∂<sub>''i''</sub> ''&rho;''<sub>''l''</sub> − ''&rho;''<sub>''i''</sub> ''&rho;''<sub>''l''</sub>)}} is constant. Substituting the above identity into the Riemann tensor as given above, it follows that the chart domain has constant sectional curvature {{math|−{{sfrac|1|''n''}}''g''<sup>''il''</sup>(∂<sub>''i''</sub> ''&rho;''<sub>''l''</sub> − ''&rho;''<sub>''i''</sub> ''&rho;''<sub>''l''</sub>)}}. By connectedness of the manifold, this local constancy implies global constancy.

Beltrami's theorem may be phrased in the language of [[geodesic map]]s: if given a geodesic map between pseudo-Riemannian manifolds, one manifold has constant curvature if and only if the other does.
